CRLA 344/2018
Hon’ble N.S. Dhanik, J.
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate, for 
the appellant/applicant. 
Mr. J.S. Virk, AGA, for the State. 
Applicant has been convicted for 
the offences under Sections 363, 376 IPC 
and 3/4 of the Protection of Children from 
Sexual Offences Act. 
Learned Counsel for the appellant 
contends that the Court below has erred in 
convicting the appellant. 
Learned State Counsel opposed the 
bail application by contending that the 
present appellant has committed very 
heinous crime and the victim is a minor 
girl and after trial the appellant stood 
convicted and has been sentenced to 
rigorous imprisonment for seven years for 
the offences under the POCSO Act. 
Considering the facts and 
circumstances of the case and on perusal 
of the materials on the record and also 
considering the nature of offences, this 
Court is not inclined to grant bail to the 
accused applicant. 
Bail application (CRMA 
11087/2018) is rejected. 
Urgency application (IA 751/2019) 
stands disposed of. 
 
 (N.S. Dhanik, J.) 
 Vacation Judge
 18.1.2019
Prabodh

CRMA No. 43/2020 (Short Term Bail Application)
IN
CRLA No. 344 of 2018
Hon’ble N.S. Dhanik, J.
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate for the 
appellant.
Mrs. Geeta Parihar, Brief Holder for the 
State of Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Learned counsel for the appellant 
contends that the marriage of the appellant 
and prosecutrix is scheduled to be held on 
18.01.2020, therefore, he may be granted short 
term bail for a period of one month.
Learned State Counsel admits this fact 
that the marriage of appellant and proseuctrix 
is scheduled to be held on 18.01.2020.
Considering the facts and circumstances
of the case, this Court is of the view that the 
appellant should be granted short term bail 
for a period of one month.
Consequently, let the appellant be 
enlarged on short term bail only for a period 
of one month from the date of his release, on 
his executing personal bond with two reliable 
sureties each of the like amount to the 
satisfaction of the Court concerned. 
It is directed that, on expiry of one 
month, the appellant shall surrender before 
the Superintendent of the Jail concerned.
Short term bail application stands 
disposed of accordingly.
Let a certified copy of this order be 
issued to the learned counsel for the parties, 
today itself, on payment of usual charges.
 
 (N.S. Dhanik, J.) 
 10.01.2020
A.kaur

Second Bail Application No. 3609 of 2019 
 In 
CRLA No. 344 of 2018 
Hon’ble N.S. Dhanik, J . 
(Via Video Conferencing) 
Mr. M.S. Pal, Senior Advocate 
assisted by Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate 
for the appellant. 
Mrs. Pushpa Bhatt, Deputy 
Advocate General along with Mr. Dinesh 
Chauhan and Mr. Balwinder Singh, Brief 
Holders for the State of Uttarakhand. 
This is the second bail application. 
The first bail application was rejected on 
18.01.2019 on merits. 
Learned counsel for the appellant 
would submit that the appellant has 
served almost half of the sentence i.e. 
three years four months. He further 
submits that that if the present appellant 
is granted bail from this Court he will 
fully cooperate with the appeal and will 
not misuse the same. 
Learned State Counsel opposed the 
bail application but admits the fact that 
the appellant has served almost half of 
the sentence i.e. three years four months. 
Having heard learned Counsel for 
the parties and considered the facts and 
circumstances of the case, I am of the 
opinion that the appellant deserves bail 
at this Stage. Hence, the bail application 
is allowed. 
Let the appellant be released on 
bail, on executing a personal bond and 
furnishing two reliable sureties, each of 
like amount, to the satisfaction of Court 
concerned. 
 (N.S. Dhanik, J.) 
 05.11.2020 SB

CRLA No. 344 of 2018
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. M.S. Pal, learned Senior 
Advocate assisted by Mr. Vikramaditya 
Shah, learned counsel for the appellant.
2. Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned Dy. A.G. 
with Mr. Sandeep Sharma and Mr. Deepak 
Bhardwaj, learned Brief Holders for the 
State.
3. Ms. Medha Pande, learned counsel 
for respondent no. 2.
4. The present appeal has been 
preferred against the judgment passed by 
the Trial Court dated 12.10.2018 in S.S.T.
No. 36 of 2017, State vs. Pradeep Kumar 
whereby the present appellant has been 
convicted under Section 363, 376 IPC read 
with Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act. The 
appellant was enlarged on bail on 
07.11.2020, by the coordinate Bench of 
this Court by observing therein that at the 
time of the incident the prosecutrix was 17 
years of age and in her statement 
recorded under Section 161 and 164 
Cr.P.C. she has categorically stated that 
she went with the appellant at her own will 
and she married with the appellant. It has 
been further observed that the medical 
report also does not suggest commission 
of offence of rape. 
5. Now the compounding application 
has been moved with this contention that 
the appellant married with the 
respondent- victim on 18.01.2020 at 
village Kaligaon, Lohaghat District 
Champawat and the said marriage is also  registered in the office of the Registrar, 
Compulsory Registration of Marriages, 
Champawat on 21.01.2020, copy of which 
is enclosed as Annexure 2 to the 
compounding application. It is also 
contended in the compounding application 
that from this marriage one female child is
also born on 19.10.2021.
6. Today, the appellant who is on bail 
as well as the victim/prosecutrix, who now 
married with the appellant on 18.01.2020 
are present before this Court along with 
minor child and this Court also interact 
with each of them particularly with the 
prosecutrix who submits that since she is 
now married with the appellant and from 
their marriage one female child is born 
and she is living happily with the 
appellant, therefore, the order of 
conviction be set aside and the appellant 
be acquitted otherwise it will spoil their 
married life.
7. Per contra, Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, 
learned Dy. Advocate General for the 
State seriously object on the compounding 
application by placing reliance on the 
judgment of Hon’ble Apex Court in Suo 
Motu Writ Petition (C) No. 3 of 2023 
decided on 20.08.2024.
8. Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned Dy. 
Advocate General with Mr. Sandeep 
Sharma, learned Brief Holder prays for 
and is granted three weeks’ time to file 
objection. One week thereafter is granted 
to the learned counsel for the appellant to 
file response to the said objection.
9. List this case on 08.11.2024.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
22.10.2024
Parul
